A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a new model, which is a variant of the multi-matrix factorization model, that is able to learn a different set of parameters for every target relation, but still shares a set of parameters among the different targets, thus being able to scale up to very large datasets.

, in order to obtain better predictions on specific target relations, one should not optimize the sum of the loss over all relations, but the sum of the individual losses over all relations. 2 Multi-matrix factorization approaches are widely used for multi-relational prediction tasks such as link and triple prediction in the context of Linked Open Data ( LOD) and recommender systems.

, for the task of multi-target link prediction, it is better to learn a model for each target relation separately, and that this can be done in a computationally efficient way by coupling the models with a set of shared parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to optimize a factorization model for a specific relation, it is not necessary to have access to the data for this relation only.
, for multi-relational data, it is better to optimize each target relation separately than to optimize the model for a compromise on all target relations at the same time.
, in order to achieve the best performance for a given multi-relational data mining task, the model needs to be optimized specifically for the task.
